questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

A tallest man that I have ever seen works in our coal mine.
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'A tallest man'. 

Key Points

  • The erroneous Part 'A tallest man' should be 'The tallest man'. 
  • The given sentence is an example of a Superlative Degree. 
  • We know that the definite article 'the' is always used before a superlative degree. Here, in the given question 'tallest' is a superlative degree of 'tall'. 
  • Superlative Degree: This degree denotes the highest degree of quality and is used when one thing/person is compared to all other things/ persons. 
    • Example: Mohan is the smartest boy in the class. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2. 
    ​

Correct Answer: The tallest man that I have ever seen works in our coal mine. 

Additional Information

  • When any object/person is required to be shown superior to all other objects of its category, the former should be shown as the part of the latter one. 
    • Example: 
      • Sachin Tendulkar is the greatest of all other cricketers. 
      • Sachin Tendulkar is the greatest of all cricketers.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

It is an ______ day to start your new business.
questions.s:
The blank requires an adjective to modify the noun 'day'.

Let's look at the meanings of the given options.

Auspicious: conducive to success; favourable.

Audacious: showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks.

Occasional: occurring, appearing, or done infrequently and irregularly.

Ominous: giving the worrying impression that something bad is going to happen; threateningly inauspicious.

Options (b) and (c) are eliminated as they do not provide a coherent sentence. We don't start a new business on a bad day. So, of the two options: (a) and (d), 'auspicious' is the most appropriate choice.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
